title: How a Raft leader election works
sub: Every node starts as a follower with a random timer. The first timer to expire asks for votes; whoever collects a majority becomes leader and keeps everyone calm with heartbeats.
aria: A ring of Raft nodes colored by role with vote and heartbeat messages flying between them
breakOff: Normal run: a leader is elected and heartbeats keep the cluster stable.
breakOn: The leader crashes 600 ms after it wins, and comes back 1.6 s later. Followers stop hearing heartbeats, so a new election starts.
learn: A follower that hears no heartbeat before its election timer expires becomes a candidate, bumps the term and requests votes. Each node votes once per term, and a majority wins.
Break it: followers notice within one timeout, the cluster elects a higher-term leader, and the old leader comes back as a follower.
Set the randomness to 0: every timer expires together, every node votes for itself, and nobody ever gets a majority. Random timeouts are the fix for split votes.
The strip at the bottom shows leadership over time. Red means the cluster cannot accept writes. Try a bigger latency or a smaller timeout and watch the gaps change.
Simplified: this shows leader election only (no log replication) and models a crash, not a network partition.
